title: India regain Women’s Asia Cup crown | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 14 September 2026 05:02
-     - 13

Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana put on the highest partnership in Women’s T20I tournament - 129

Chamari Athapaththu’s innings of 36 was not good enough for Sri Lanka to win

Shree Charani scalps another Sri Lankan wicket on her way to a four-wicket haul

Defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final

India regained the Women’s Asia Cup defeating defending champions Sri Lanka in convincing fashion by 72 runs in the final played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium yesterday. It was overall, India’s eighth Women’s Asia Cup title.

Chasing 184 was always going to be a steep hill to climb for Sri Lanka, and India’s disciplined attack made it virtually impossible. Sri Lanka lost wickets in clusters, having no answers to the spin and guile of Shree Charani, who delivered a game-changing spell of 4/22. The experienced Deepti Sharma provided brilliant support, picking up 3 crucial wickets for 19 to finish as the leading wicket-taker of the tournament.

The Indian spinners operated in tandem to completely freeze the scoring through the middle overs, and as the required rate skyrocketed, Sri Lanka simply collapsed under the pressure of trying to hit out.

Sri Lanka entered the final unbeaten on the back of several middle-order rescue acts, but yesterday there was no coming back. India were by far the most dominant team in the tournament.

Batting first India put up a daunting target for Sri Lanka. The tone was set right at the top by Smriti Mandhana (59 off 39 balls, 5 fours, 3 sixes) and Shafali Verma (68 off 39 balls, 9 fours, 2 sixes) blazed through the powerplay, laying a rock-solid foundation with a sensational opening partnership of 129 - the highest in Women’s T20I tournament final.

Once the openers departed, Sri Lanka pulled things back admirably. Runs dried up in the middle overs, and a cluster of quick wickets threatened to derail the momentum. But a late flourish pushed India to a formidable total. As for Sri Lanka, their bowling lacked bite for large spells, offering far too many loose deliveries that the Indian batters gleefully punished.

Scores: 

India Women 183-5 (20) (Smriti Mandhana 59, Shafali Verma 68, Mithali Ayodhya 1/33) defeated Sri Lanka Women 111 (20) (Chamari Athapaththu 36, Vishmi Gunaratne 20, Nilakshika Silva 22, Shree Charani 4/20, Deepti Sharma 3/19)

title: Up Country Lions beat Renown 2-0 to maintain remarkable record | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 14 September 2026 04:58
-     - 39

Red Star hold Colombo FC to 2-2 draw

By Althaf Nawaz

Up Country Lions’s Mohamed Ishan, who was instrumental in scoring one of their goals against Renown SC which earned him Player of the Match, celebrates after scoring

Table leaders Up Country Lions SC maintained their superiority with a 2-0 victory over Renown SC at the Sugathadasa Stadium yesterday, remaining unbeaten in the second edition of the Super League Soccer Tournament conducted by Football Sri Lanka.

Undoubtedly the best skilled team in the fray, the boys from Up Country dominated proceedings from the start, but lady luck deserted them in the early stages of the game and they were unable to score. However, as the game wore on, they managed to boot two swashbuckling goals in each half, which enabled them to notch up their ninth consecutive win.

They have now secured 27 points and is the only unbeaten team at the conclusion of the preliminary round, which is a remarkable effort.

They have now qualified for the Super Six round, which is scheduled to kick off in a few weeks.

After some anxious moments of play, neither side was able to break the deadlock until the final quarter of the first half. Up Country Lions striker Mohamed Ishan finally found the net off a well-executed header after latching on to a nippy pass from his co-striker Mohamed Akib to go for lemons 1-0.

After the turnaround, Renown – fielding a young side – found their rhythm in the initial quarter, but failed to maintain the momentum and ran out of firepower due to poor physical fitness, which gave their rivals an opportunity to capitalise on the situation.

The winners placed the final nail on the coffin when Akib put up a belligerent performance to increase their lead with a spectacular goal which made the scoreline 2-0, which remained until the long whistle.

Red Star SC vs. Colombo FC

Meanwhile, on Saturday at the same venue, Red Star SC managed to force a 2-all draw against Colombo FC after trailing 2-0 in the first half. 

Colombo FC have only themselves to blame for their dismal performance in the second half, where some of their players opted to play rough, which resulted in one player being sent off after being shown two yellow cards. They had a lead at the breather and scored their second goal early in the second half. 

But the lads from Dharga Town surged into the game quite magnificently to hold their nerve and scored twice, one of them off a penalty.

Both teams have qualified for the round of six.

title: Pathirage bags Gold, makes history with 90m breach at World Athletics Ultimate Championship | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 14 September 2026 04:57
-     - 24

Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage

Sri Lankan javelin star Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage capped his remarkable season with another major victory, winning the men’s javelin at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship Budapest 26, yesterday becoming the first athlete to throw beyond 90 metres on Hungarian soil.

Pathirage produced a winning throw of 91.09m to claim the title, a mark that also stood as the historic first for the venue.

The victory adds another milestone to a stunning season for the Sri Lankan, who had won 11 of his 12 competitions before arriving in Budapest. He also won the Diamond League Final after recording a world-leading 92.62m in Rome and followed it with a 92.07m victory in Zurich.

Pathirage made a slow start in Budapest, opening with 75.89m, while Germany’s Julian Weber immediately moved into the lead with 84.09m. Anderson Peters of Grenada then took control in the second round with 86.18m. Pathirage responded with 85.69m before improving to 87.11m in the third round to move into first place. Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem managed a season’s best of 81.49m but finished outside the top four after three rounds.

Pathirage saved his best for last. Throwing first in the final round, the Sri Lankan unleashed a 91.09m effort to pull clear of his rivals and secure another prestigious title. Peters finished with 82.63m, while Weber’s final throw measured 78.75m.

title: Viren, Dumindu and Ranithma vie for medals at Asian Games in Badminton | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 14 September 2026 04:54
-     - 18

From left: Yohners Rambothan of Indonesia as Coach, Dumindu Abeywickrama, Viren Nettasinghe, and Ranithma Liyanage

Sri Lanka will be represented by three top shuttlers – namely Viren Nettasinghe, Dumindu Abeywickrama and Ranithma Liyanage – at the 20th Asian Games 2026, to be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from 19 September to 4 October.

With high medal hopes, the three shuttlers will compete in individual events at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium in Aichi, where badminton events of the Asian Games will be played from 20 to 29 September. Viren and Dumindu will compete in the men’s singles event, which begins on 25 September, while Ranithma will also take the field on the same day in the women’s singles event. Both events will run concurrently, but the women’s singles will reach its quarter-finals on 26 September, while, with a longer list of entries, the men’s singles will reach its quarter-final stage on 27 September. The finals of both events will be held on 29 September.

Viren, 23, the youngest Sri Lankan to qualify for the Paris 2024 Olympics, is currently Sri Lanka’s top-ranked men’s singles shuttler alongside Dumindu, who has been in prime form during recent international competitions played since last year. Ranithma is currently Sri Lanka’s top seed in women’s singles. The three-member badminton team will be accompanied by Yohners Rambothan of Indonesia as Coach and Team Official.

A Division Champions – Team Seylan Bank

B Division Champions – Team CIAP

C Division Champions – Team John Keells

The sixth 9-A-Side Hockey Tournament, organised by the Mercantile Hockey Association (MHA), concluded successfully on 22 August at the Colombo Astro Turf, Colombo 7, with leading corporate teams competing across the A, B, and C Divisions. The tournament was sponsored by Janashakthi Group as the Title Sponsor.

Seylan Bank emerged as the A Division champions, defeating Sampath Bank 1-0 in a closely contested final. The winning goal was scored by Seylan Bank Captain Jiffery Irshad, while Sandaru Madushan was named the Best Player of the A Division.

The B Division saw CIAP claim the championship with a convincing 3-1 victory over Brown & Company. Sandun Gajanayake scored two goals for CIAP, while Nethmina Dharmakeerthi also found the net. Pathum Prabodha scored the only goal for Browns. Nethmina Dharmakeerthi of CIAP was named the Best Player of the B Division.

Meanwhile, John Keells Holdings secured the C Division championship after defeating David Pieris Motor Company 1-0, with Lasitha Manchanayake scoring the decisive goal. Lasitha Manchanayake was also named the Best Player of the C Division.

The tournament was graced by Chief Guest Janashakthi Group Vice President – Marketing Sohan Colabage and Manager – Brand Activations Yehan Hadapangoda, whose presence added further significance to the successful conclusion of the tournament.

The MHA extends its sincere appreciation to Janashakthi Group, the Title Sponsor, for its valued support and commitment towards the development of hockey in Sri Lanka. The Association also extends its gratitude to all participating teams, players, officials, volunteers, and supporters, as well as the media partners and media personnel, for their valuable coverage and support.

title: SSC into another Major Club final    | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 14 September 2026 04:37
-     - 16

Tamil Union qualify with win over CCC in Super Over

 Kusal Mendis, Binura Fernando make their mark from injuries

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

SSC in their return to Major Club cricket reached their second successive final when they beat arch rivals NCC by 46 runs under lights at the R Premadasa Cricket Stadium while in the other semi-final, also a day-night affair played at the SSC grounds, Tamil Union beat defending champions CCC in the Super Over after the two teams had tied on a similar score at 193-6 yesterday.

SSC and Tamil Union will meet in the final at the R Premadasa Cricket Stadium under lights on 16 September.

The semi-finals were notable for the return of two Sri Lankan players who were forced to miss the three-match T20I series in England due to injuries. White ball Captain Kusal Mendis making his first appearance since being laid low with a hamstring injury hit a sparkling half-century off 35 balls (3 fours, 2 sixes) for SSC, while left-arm fast-bowler Binura Fernando took 3/30 to peg down CCC to a total of 193-6 and force a Super Over where he dismissed the two CCC batsmen off successive balls leaving Tamil Union to score one run for victory which they did.

Apart from Kusal Mendis’ half-century, Nuwanidu Fernando also scored a fifty – 30 balls (4 fours, 3 sixes) supported by 35 and 36 from openers Vishad Randika and Avishka Fernando that enabled SSC reach 196-4. NCC failed to get the momentum going in their innings and with the exception of a 53-runs stand for the second wicket between Niroshan Dickwella (38 off 21 balls) and Kavin Bandara (41 off 34) never looked like challenging SSC’s total. NCC were dismissed for 150 with an over to spare with spinners Malsha Fernando (3/22) and Kavindu Nadeeshan (3/25) capturing a major share of the wickets.

An all-round batting performance saw Tamil Union hit up 193-6 after being invited to bat first. Thanuka Dabare set the pace for them top scoring with 42 off 17 balls (6 fours, 2 sixes) followed by contributions of 36, 33 and 32 from Sharujan Shanmuganathan, Thevindu Senarathne and Sachitha Jayathilake respectively.

Nishan Madushka played a lone hand in CCC’s reply of 193-6. A failure in Test cricket he made a statement in white ball cricket with back to back centuries. He followed his knock of 114* against Ace Capital CC in the quarter-final on Wednesday with 109* off 65 balls (7 fours, 6 sixes). The second highest score was Dulnith Sigera’s 31.

title: Sri Lanka reach seventh Asia Cup final | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 12 September 2026 00:49
-     - 21

Defending champions Sri Lanka reached their seventh Women’s Asia Cup final when they beat Pakistan by four wickets with eight balls to spare in a closely contested second semi-final played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium yesterday.

Sri Lanka will meet seven-times champions India in the final on Sunday.

Set a target of 131 Sri Lanka stumbled to 33-4 with Pakistan captain Fatima Sana leading the way with a double wicket first over. A 67-run stand for the fifth wicket between Harshitha Samarawickrama (36) and Imesha Dulani (33) brought Sri Lanka back into contention.

But Sana had not finished yet for when she came for a second spell she once again struck twice to send back both set batters. However the experienced Nilakshika Silva (18*) and Kaushini Nuthyangana (10*) kept cool heads to see Sri Lanka over the line.   

Sana led Pakistan from the front and guided her team to 130 after being invited to bat first. Pakistan lost Muneeba Ali early, but Shawaal Zulfiqar and Gull Feroza then chipped in with scores in the 20s. Pakistan were 92-5 at the end of 16 overs when Tuba Hassan joined Sana, and the duo put on an all-important unbeaten 38-run stand off just 24 deliveries. Sana scored 47 off 36 balls and made sure Pakistan touched the 130-run mark. She took the Player of the Match award for her superb all-round contribution.

Scores: 

Pakistan Women 130-5 (20) (Shawaal Zulfiqar 24, Gull Feroza 21, Fatima Sana 47*, Chamari Athapaththu 2/24, Chamudi Praboda 2/25) lost to Sri Lanka Women 134-6 (18.4) (Imesh Dulani 24, Harshitha Samarawickrama 36, Kavisha Dilhari 33, Fatima Sana 4/38)
